headline: Town Meeting approved $4.5 million to replace the Neary School roof and $175,000 for a renovation study, rejecting school consolidation alternatives.
synopsis: Special Town Meeting voters authorized $4.5 million in borrowing to replace the Neary Elementary School roof and approved $175,000 for a renovation feasibility study, while defeating proposals to study school consolidation. The Select Board and School Committee convened the following night to begin drafting roof bid documents ahead of a May 12 ballot vote required to finalize the borrowing. The Select Board also deliberated the draft FY27 budget, which currently projects a 4.9 percent property tax increase. Elsewhere, the Municipal Technology Committee supported a $25,000 phone system upgrade, and the Historical Commission addressed insurance concerns for historic district homeowners.

highlights.title: Neary School roof replacement borrowing
highlights.why: Voters approved borrowing up to $4.5 million to replace Neary's failing roof during summer 2026, though the project requires a subsequent town election ballot vote to take effect.

highlights.title: Neary School renovation feasibility study
highlights.why: Town Meeting voted to transfer $175,000 from Free Cash to evaluate modernization and targeted code-compliance options to extend Neary's operating life.

highlights.title: Rejection of Trottier and Finn expansion study
highlights.why: Voters rejected an article proposing up to $500,000 to study closing Neary and adding onto Trottier and Finn, citing septic limits, traffic congestion, and site constraints.

highlights.title: FY27 operating budget deliberations
highlights.why: Select Board members reviewed a draft level-services budget projecting a 4.9 percent property tax increase and debated whether to pursue cuts to lower the tax impact on residents.

highlights.title: Post-Town Meeting Neary bid preparations
highlights.why: The Select Board and School Committee voted to direct the superintendent to draft bid documents immediately so roof construction can begin promptly following the May ballot vote.

highlights.title: Homeowner insurance concerns in historic districts
highlights.why: The commission prepared clarification letters for insurers, explaining that National Register listings and town plaque designations impose no mandatory rebuilding or renovation restrictions.
